reason: Start with the bone-cell lineage to connect the existing stem cells to living bone.
expectation: I expect the conditions to produce bone-lineage cells over time, though their precise role in the construction is unclear.

alternatives.reason: Mineralizing the collagen framework also seems useful for building strong bones, but I want to establish the living cells first.

effect: The lineage produces matrix-making osteoblasts and embedded osteocytes, clarifying how living cells fit into mature bone.
reaction: The distinction between the two bone-cell roles is useful; the precursor terms are less explained.
reason: Combine the collagen framework and mineral to build the structural material of the arm bones.
expectation: I expect a mineralized bone framework, with collagen and mineral contributing different properties.

alternatives.reason: Supplying the bone cells with blood vessels also advances the living-bone goal, but I want to build the framework first.

effect: The framework now combines collagen's toughness with mineral's resistance to compression; bone cells can be added to it.
reaction: The contrast between the two materials makes their contributions clear.
reason: Add the bone cells to the mineralised framework to build living bone.
expectation: I expect the cells to be shown within the mineralised arm bones, though they may still need a blood supply.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the cells to blood vessels also addresses the supply goal, but I want to assemble the bone first.

effect: The bone framework now contains embedded cells, and the unfilled vessel outline points to the remaining blood-supply detail.
reaction: The cutaway makes clear that this is an assembly of mature bone rather than a developmental sequence.
reason: Add blood vessels to complete the supplied living-bone construction.
expectation: I expect vessels to be shown supplying the bone cells within the arm bones.

alternatives.reason: The joint sleeve and lining also advance a goal, but I want to finish the bone first.

effect: The bones now combine mineralised matrix, living cells and a blood supply; the next goal is to connect them into a movable joint.
reaction: The nested cutaway usefully distinguishes the vessel from the channels connecting cell spaces.
reason: Line the fibrous sleeve to advance the joint capsule goal.
expectation: I expect a lined capsule with synovial membrane on the sleeve's inner surface.

alternatives.reason: Cartilage on the bone ends also seems necessary for the joint, but I want to complete the capsule first.

effect: The lined capsule is complete, with its secretions contributing to fluid in the joint cavity.
reaction: The lining's position and contribution to joint fluid are clear.
reason: Add cartilage to the living bones; it is the only available combination and advances the joint goal.
expectation: I expect cartilage to cover the bone ends where they meet at the elbow.

effect: The bone ends now have smooth cartilage caps, ready to be enclosed by the capsule.
reaction: The sliding inset makes the cartilage's position clear.
reason: Combine the capped bones with the capsule to assemble the joint; this is the only available combination.
expectation: I expect the capsule to surround the cartilage-covered elbow surfaces and joint cavity.

effect: The capsule now encloses the cartilage-covered bone ends, with lining fluid helping the surfaces glide.
reaction: The connection between the lining, fluid and sliding surfaces is clear.
reason: Add the ligaments to support the elbow; this is the only available combination.
expectation: I expect the ligaments to reinforce the joint while allowing movement.

effect: The ligaments complete the supported joint, allowing bending while resisting sideways movement; all goals are complete.
reaction: The opposing arrows make the ligaments’ role clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the living bone cutaway was most worthwhile: it brought mineral-reinforced collagen, embedded cells and blood supply together in distinct locations.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding cells to the mineralised framework felt somewhat repetitive between making the cells and completing the supplied bone, although it clarified the mature-tissue assembly.

surprise.text: The lineage inset distinguished matrix-producing osteoblasts from embedded osteocytes, though mesodermal and mesenchymal precursors were not explained.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless; the late sequence was straightforward, with only one combination offered at each step.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the planned cutaways connected structure and function clearly, and I would be curious to see how muscles move the completed joint.
